key_insight: The paper unifies multiple "butterfly effect" regimes in turbulence using finite-size Lyapunov exponents, showing how predictability changes from small-scale chaos to large-scale stochasticity.
engineering_relevance: It helps quantify forecasting limits in high-Reynolds-number flows, which is useful for turbulence prediction, modeling, and uncertainty-aware engineering design.
method: Uses the Finite Size Lyapunov Exponent (FSLE) to measure perturbation growth versus scale.
Analyzes the Sabra shell model with added thermal noise to bridge classical Lyapunov chaos and large-scale predictability.
Uses the Kraichnan model to illustrate Lagrangian spontaneous stochasticity and contrasts it with localized sub-dissipative perturbations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic synthesis supported by FSLE-based analysis of the Sabra shell model and the Kraichnan model, rather than a single experimental dataset.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on idealized models and FSLE interpretation, so transfer to real turbulent flows may require careful validation.
paper_title: The real butterfly effect: from the pop culture to mathematics and physics
